# Triage labels

The skills speak in two category roles and five state roles. Every triaged issue carries
exactly one category role and one state role. These tables map each role to the label this
repository uses. Descriptions are creation defaults and intended purposes; the maintainer
is habit. Preserve existing same-name, same-purpose labels even when their descriptions
differ. Escalate a purpose conflict to habit before changing a label or using it for a
different role. When a skill names a role, use its label from these tables, and keep
unrelated labels.

## Category roles

`bug` means something is broken; `enhancement` means a new feature or improvement.

| Role in mattpocock/skills | Label here | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bug` | `bug` | Something isn't working |
| `enhancement` | `enhancement` | New feature or request |

## State roles

| Role in mattpocock/skills | Label here | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs-triage` | `needs-triage` | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue |
| `needs-info` | `needs-info` | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| `ready-for-agent` | `ready-for-agent` | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent |
| `ready-for-human` | `ready-for-human` | Requires human implementation |
| `wontfix` | `wontfix` | Will not be actioned |

## `ready-for-agent`

It means habit approved the issue as a ticket and it can be dispatched. It authorizes nothing
by itself.

- **Dispatch** is habit naming the ticket in a start instruction, which starts its Builder.
  No comment marks it, and the Builder's claim follows (`issue-tracker.md`, Tickets).
- A spec loses the label once its tickets exist, unless habit approved it for whole-spec
  delivery: then the spec keeps it and its tickets never take it (`planner.md`, Specs).
